+---
+## What
+In the full `swift test` run of 2026-10-03 (task ^mc84eb7), this test failed one time at `AgentProcessTeardownTests.swift`: `Expectation failed: !StdioChild.isInProcessTable(pid: child.pid)`. The same test passed when `swift test --filter AgentProcessTeardownTests` ran it alone. The failing change did not touch `AgentProcess.swift` or this test.
+
+Probable cause: `TeardownTestDeadline.reapTimeLimit` is 200 ms. Under the load of the full parallel run, the reading child can need more than 200 ms to see end of file, exit, and be collected. `AgentProcessState.reap(pid:)` then stops its `WNOHANG` poll at the deadline, and the child is still in the process table when the test reads it.
+
+- [ ] Find the true cause (load, pid reuse, or zombie timing) with a test that fails on purpose.
+- [ ] Make the test deterministic: it must not depend on the load of the machine. Do not only raise the time limit.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] The full `swift test` run passes this test every time.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd`.
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m41e7npm7cywb39wbr31hdya
+  text: |-
+    Research done.
+
+    - `AgentProcessState.reap(pid:)` polls `waitpid(WNOHANG)` every 10 ms and stops at `reapTimeLimit`. The test gives 200 ms. The test then asserts that the child is gone. So the test passes only when `/bin/cat` reads EOF, exits, and is collected in less than 200 ms. That is a timing guess, not an event.
+    - Two things can make the exit late: (1) load of the full parallel run; (2) a race on the descriptors. `spawnInThisProcessGroup` calls `pipe()` and then `fcntl(FD_CLOEXEC)`. Between the two calls, a parallel test can spawn a child (for example the `sleep 300` child of the sibling test). That child gets a copy of the write end of the cat pipe. Cat then reads no EOF until the sibling test kills its child, after its own 200 ms teardown. Both causes give "cat exits after 200 ms" and the reported failure.
+    - Pid reuse and zombie timing are not the cause: `waitpid` collects the child (no zombie stays), and macOS gives pids in sequence.
+    - Plan: (a) RED test with a child that exits 0.5 s after EOF (a deterministic model of a late exit) under the 200 ms limit; it must fail. (b) The reaping tests use the production limit `AgentProcessState.defaultReapTimeLimit`, so the pass is decided by the event (the child exits and `waitpid` collects it), and the limit is only the hang bound. (c) The test helper spawns with `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT`, so its child gets no descriptor of a parallel test.
+    - Production `AgentProcess.createPipe()` has the same `pipe()`/`fcntl` window. Its doc says no child can inherit the ends, which is not true for a spawn on another thread. I record this as a new task; it is out of scope here.
